title: SDK Integration Contract and Bundle Validator Playbook
author: Maya Patel
summary: A prescriptive playbook for validating SDK integration contracts and packaging a distribution bundle for safe rollout. Defines checks, CLI validator flows, common failure modes with canonical fixes, and a lightweight gating policy for dev and release pipelines.
body:
Overview

This playbook documents the SDK integration contract checks and the bundle-validator we run as part of DX CI and release pipelines. The goal is to catch integration regressions (API surface changes, telemetry gaps, schema drift) before SDK packages are published to registries or distributed to customers. The validator is intentionally lightweight so it can run in pull-request checks and in nightly pipelines.

When to use

- On every PR that changes: public SDK surface, request/response shapes, telemetry events, or packaged assets (wheel/tarball/npm).
- Before cutting an SDK release candidate (rc) and prior to publishing to internal registries.
- As part of customer-specific integration checks for Dedicated/Private deployment handoffs.

Definitions

- Integration Contract: stable request/response JSON schema, named API endpoints and client method signatures, error-code set, and telemetry event list.
- Bundle: packaged distribution (e.g., pip wheel, npm package) plus shipping artifacts (README, changelog, schemas, sample prompts, telemetry spec).
- Validator: CLI tool that runs a suite of static and dynamic checks against a candidate bundle and a baseline contract.

Roles & Ownership

- SDK Owner: responsible for updating contract files, implementing fixes, and interpreting validator failures. (Default: dx-sdk team)
- DX Validator Maintainer: keeps the validator code, canonical rule set, and baseline contracts up to date. (Default: devx-infra)
- Release Manager: authorizes release when validator green.

Gating policy (recommended)

- PR gate (fast): run fast checks (lint, public API diff, required files present). Must pass before merge.
- RC gate (full): run dynamic tests (end-to-end example against staging runtime, telemetry sample verification, packaging verification). Must pass to publish.

Quick checklist (PR-level)

1. public_api.yaml present and valid
2. schema/response/ and schema/request/ updated only via ADR or with migration notes
3. telemetry-events.yaml updated for any trackable changes
4. sample-usage.* updated and executed in CI smoke test
5. package artifact builds and checksum (sha256) verified

Validator commands (examples)

# Install validator (pyproject)
python -m pip install git+https://github.com/redwood-inference/dx-validator.git@main

# Run full validator against a wheel file
dx-validate bundle --bundle dist/redwood_sdk-1.2.0-py3-none-any.whl --baseline contracts/baseline-2026-01.json --staging-url https://staging.api.redwood.ai

# Run incremental PR checks (fast mode)
dx-validate quick --src ./src/redwood_sdk --public-api public_api.yaml --telemetry telemetry-events.yaml

What the validator checks

Static checks (fast)
- public API surface diff (added/removed/changed methods and parameters)
- presence and lint of public_api.yaml, telemetry-events.yaml, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE
- packaging manifest sanity: pyproject.toml / package.json fields, required files included

Schema checks (medium)
- response/request JSON schema compatibility against baseline (backwards-compatible additions only unless flagged)
- status/error codes set does not remove codes used in baseline
- example payloads validate against declared schemas

Dynamic checks (slow)
- smoke invocation against a staging runtime and validation of shaped outputs
- telemetry event emission check: sample calls must produce expected events within 30s window to the telemetry-proxy test endpoint
- integration example scripts run and exit 0

Failure modes and canonical fixes

1) Public API removed or renamed
Symptom: validator flags removed public methods or parameter changes.
Fix: Revert rename or add compatibility shim; create ADR for breaking change and prepare migration notes; increment major version if intentional.

2) Schema drift that breaks customers
Symptom: response schema removed required fields.
Fix: Reintroduce fields, add deprecation warnings, or publish a compatibility adapter; update schema migration notes and create an eval test that exercises edge case.

3) Telemetry not emitted or missing fields
Symptom: telemetry-events.yaml mismatches produced events or sample invocation produces no events to test endpoint.
Fix: Ensure telemetry instrumentation code triggers events; validate flush behavior in async clients; add a test that asserts event attributes.

4) Packaging missing files (README, LICENSE, sample prompts)
Symptom: artifact lacks declared files; customers report confusing install or usage.
Fix: Update pyproject/package.json include list and add CI gate that validates artifact contents and checksum.

Canonical fixes snippets

- Add compatibility shim example (Python):
from typing import Any

# Old signature: def summarize(text: str) -> str
# New signature: def summarize(text: str, model: Optional[str] = None) -> str

def summarize(text: Any, model: Any = None):
    # shim: accept both calls and forward to new implementation
    return _impl_summarize(str(text), model=model)

- Telemetry flush example (async client)
await client.emit_event("generation_request", {"model": model_name})
await client.flush(timeout_seconds=5)

Packaging validation example (CI YAML excerpt)

steps:
  - run: python -m pip wheel . -w dist/
  - run: dx-validate bundle --bundle dist/*.whl --baseline contracts/baseline-2026-01.json

E2E smoke test (minimal)

1. Start local telemetry-proxy (docker run -p 9001:9001 redwood/telemetry-proxy:test)
2. Install candidate wheel into virtualenv
3. Run sample-usage/smoke_invoke.py which: creates a client, calls generate(sample_prompt), asserts non-empty text, and polls telemetry-proxy for event.

Metrics and SLOs for validator

- PR quick-check median time: < 90s (target)
- RC full-check median time: < 900s (target)
- False positive rate goal: < 2% per quarter
- Coverage: validator suite must exercise at least 3 canonical example flows per SDK (generation, embeddings, health-check)

Telemetry expectations (for sample invocations)

- Event names: generation.request, generation.response, sdk.install, sdk.error
- Required fields on generation.request: client_id, request_id, model, prompt_length, timestamp
- Required fields on generation.response: request_id, latency_ms, tokens_generated, status

Rollout guidance

- Canary: publish RC to internal channel and run the RC full-check against a reserved staging project for 24 hours. Monitor: SDK error-rate, telemetry missing-field rate, and runtime latency delta.
- Gradual: 10% -> 50% -> 100% distribution over 72 hours if all metrics stable.

Incident triage checklist (validator failures post-release)

1. Reproduce failure with the same bundle and baseline locally using dx-validate reproduce --bundle <bundle> --baseline <baseline>
2. Capture logs from telemetry-proxy and staging runtime; include request_id from failing test
3. Patch and run RC full-check; if green, promote new RC through canary flow

FAQ

Q: Who updates baseline contracts?
A: DX Validator Maintainers update baselines when there is an authorized platform or API change. SDK teams must notify maintainers via #dx-validator and attach ADRs for breaking changes.

Q: Can we disable a check for a quick hotfix?
A: Only the Release Manager can temporarily disable a check. Document the exception in the PR and re-enable within one business day. Exceptions must be included in the release notes.

Appendix: public_api.yaml minimal example

# public_api.yaml
methods:
  - name: generate
    description: "Synchronous text generation method"
    params:
      - name: prompt
        type: string
        required: true
      - name: model
        type: string
        required: false
    returns:
      type: object
      schema: response/generate.json

Appendix: telemetry-events.yaml minimal example

# telemetry-events.yaml
events:
  - name: generation.request
    required_fields: [client_id, request_id, model, prompt_length, timestamp]
  - name: generation.response
    required_fields: [request_id, latency_ms, tokens_generated, status]

This document is intended to be the canonical playbook for validating SDK integration contracts and bundle distribution. Maintain the baseline contracts in contracts/ and open PRs against dx-validator for new validation rules.
